posts.name: Mantasha fatma
posts.cooked: What is the best way to prepare for OPPE—not just to pass, but to score good marks?

posts.name: Praveen Mishra
posts.cooked:
TA’s reply to the same question:

For OPPE practice, you can rely on the oppe-practice-* questions in the course VM. The VM has 130+ questions for you to practice. Solving 80-100 of them will easily build your foundations and help you score in the OPPE.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
The best thing is to practice & do lots of practice. As I have already mentioned in several TA sessions that you have to get your core concepts cleared and practice enough to get the commands in your muscle memory.

As mentioned above, yes the VM has a lot of practice questions, you can do that. Apart from that if you want get your basics right you can practice on hackkerank. https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/shell

Apart from that you can create your own file (get data rows from Kaggle preferably .csv) in the field of your interest. Try file manipulation in different ways & you can also check out this resource →

  • System Commands | Jan 2026 | References | Guidelines
  • T12026 | Resources for Shell Scripting and other utilities

Thanks & Regards,
Swati Jain

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Shell completions are completely normal and allowed. Course VM also has them by pressing Tab.

posts.name: Diptanshu Suraj dube
posts.cooked: will the question format have the Motivation section or is it given for a reference on these PYQs? also will there be a cheatsheet ? If yes, what all details and commands will be there on that?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Motivation (if applicable) will be there.

No cheatsheets, but you can refer any man page or info page. info pages for bash, grep, sed, and awk, are basically a full book so any and all required information can be referred from there.

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked:
@starfury9 you can check the above thread for the suggestions. Also check the below reply:

System commands oppe questions pattern System Commands
5 questions of equal weightage. Can be from any topic in W1-9. Usual hot topics: file manipulation pattern matching (bash or grep or sed) sed awk scripting variables other utils like find, shasum, realpath, readlink, base64, tr, paste, xxd, etc
